html:
The first Greek-speaking civilisation, in mainland Greece in the late Bronze Age, from about 1600 to 1100 BCE. It is named after Mycenae, its richest citadel, and was a world of palace kingdoms ruled by warrior kings.

The Mycenaeans learned much from Minoan Crete: art, palace life and writing. Their early rulers were buried in shaft graves at Mycenae with gold masks and weapons, found by Heinrich Schliemann in 1876. Later kings were laid in great beehive tombs.

Their world:

  • Palace centres at Mycenae, Pylos, Tiryns, Thebes and elsewhere, many behind huge "Cyclopean" walls of rough stone.
  • Scribes kept accounts on clay tablets in Linear B. Michael Ventris deciphered it in 1952 and showed that it was an early form of Greek.
  • The tablets show palaces tracking land, sheep, wool, bronze, perfumed oil and offerings to gods such as Zeus, Hera and Poseidon.
  • Around 1450 BCE they took over Knossos on Crete, and they traded across the Mediterranean, from Italy to Cyprus and the Levant.

Around 1200 BCE the palaces were burned and abandoned, part of the Late Bronze Age collapse that also brought down the Hittites and shook Egypt. The causes may include drought, earthquakes, revolts, raiders and broken trade. Writing vanished from Greece for some four centuries.

The Greeks of later times remembered this age as a time of heroes. The war against Troy, told in the Iliad of Homer, is set in it, and Agamemnon was king of Mycenae. When Greek cities rose again after 800 BCE, as the Greek city-states, they kept the language and many of the gods.
sum: The first Greek-speaking civilisation, in mainland Greece in the late Bronze Age, from about 1600 to 1100 BCE. It is named after Mycenae, its richest citadel, and was a world of palace kingdoms ruled by warrior kings.
